paragraphs: Thirteen fostering services list Liverpool as an area they cover: Liverpool City Council's own fostering service and twelve independent agencies, all shown above. The council says its children's services are responsible for more than 1,500 looked-after children in the city. Fostering for the council means caring for Liverpool children, helping them stay in their own communities, with the council's social workers behind you; an independent agency assesses, approves and supervises you itself and offers homes to children placed by councils.

Liverpool recruits through Foster4, launched in May 2024 with Cheshire East, Cheshire West and Chester, Halton, Knowsley, St Helens, Warrington and Wirral and backed by the Department for Education. At launch the eight councils had more than 4,600 children in care between them and just over 1,150 approved council foster carers, and said there was an urgent need for more. Foster4 shares training across the eight areas and uses the Mockingbird model, in which an experienced hub carer supports six to ten nearby fostering families.

After an enquiry, initial checks and a home visit, applicants take the Skills to Foster course and then a two-stage assessment, with the assessing social worker visiting about seven times, before a fostering panel, which meets at least monthly. Foster4 aims to have carers approved within four to six months of Skills to Foster. Carers already with an agency or another council can transfer, which Liverpool aims to complete in eight to twelve weeks.

Council carers get Council Tax exemption, training before and after approval, free Lifestyles gym membership and use of a holiday home at Presthaven Beach Resort, alongside skills and children's allowance payments. We do not yet have a Liverpool allowance page, so ask the council and two or three of the agencies above for their rates and compare the support each offers.
If you live near the city's edge, the pages for Knowsley, Sefton and Wirral list more services.
